The area of triangle \(ABC\) is 144. The centroid \(G\) divides each median in a 2:1 ratio. The line through \(G\) parallel to \(BC\) creates a smaller triangle \(AMN\) similar to \(ABC\) with similarity ratio \(AG/AD = 2/3\). Thus \(AN = \frac{2}{3}AC\).  
\(E\) is the midpoint of \(AC\) (since \(BE\) is a median), so \(AE = \frac{1}{2}AC\).  
Then \(EN = AN - AE = \frac{2}{3}AC - \frac{1}{2}AC = \frac{1}{6}AC\).  
Triangle \(AGC\) has area \(\frac{1}{3}\) of \(ABC\), so \([AGC] = 48\).  
Triangle \(ENG\) shares the same height from \(G\) to line \(AC\) as triangle \(AGC\), so its area is proportional to its base \(EN\):  
\([ENG] = \frac{EN}{AC} \times [AGC] = \frac{1}{6} \times 48 = 8\).  
(Note: A common mistake is to find the area of \(\triangle EMN\) instead, which is 16, but the problem asks for \(\triangle ENG\).)

Answer: 8
